value.body: Builds the parts of websites and apps that people see and use — pages, forms and dashboards — and makes them fast, accessible and consistent across devices. Employers include IT services firms, product companies, startups and GCCs. A typical day involves writing JavaScript or TypeScript components from designs, fixing bugs and reviewing code with teammates.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BCA, B.Sc (CS) or B.Tech in any branch
items.note: Demonstrated skills often count as much as the degree

items.label: Common tools
items.value: HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, a framework such as React or Angular, Git

items.label: Indian tech-sector workforce
items.note: Whole IT-BPM sector, not this role alone

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers get in through campus placement at IT services firms (often a general trainee role first, with a stack assigned after training), or by applying directly to startups and product companies with a portfolio. A few deployed projects in a public code repository and solid JavaScript fundamentals usually count more than certificates.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: A component framework such as React

value.title: At a glance
items: Growth path: developer → senior → lead, or a move into full-stack, UI engineering or design systems.
Tools change quickly; ongoing self-learning is part of the job.
Entry-level competition is high, so a visible portfolio helps.
In large service firms, freshers are often assigned a stack rather than choosing it.

competition.note: BCA graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among BCA graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
